newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong hits high on laggards buying.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong hits high on laggards buying.

text.p: Demand for blue chips property laggards boosted shares of Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd to an all time high of HK$59 at midday on Monday, up HK$1.50 or 2.61 percent from its previous close.
Volume was 3.74 million shares worth HK$219.23 million.

"Demand for blue-chips property laggards fueled demand for Cheung Kong, expecially when the stock is the cheapest in term of P.E. (price to earnings multiple) among the main blue chip property counters," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Cheung Kong's P.E. was at 11.65, compared Sun Hung Kai Properties at 18.39, Henderson Land at 12.79 and New World Development at 18.89, analysts said.
"Cheung Kong's move of participating in the property agency business also gave a short term positive stimulation to the shares," Li added.
Michael Ng from Sassoon Securities said optimism over the property market in view of the recent strong responses to flat sales also aided demand for major property counters.
